nodes.text: high-interest currencies earn their rate differential and tend not to fall by as much
carry portfolios across many currencies earned a premium, with crashes in global risk-off (Lustig & Verdelhan 2007; Menkhoff et al. 2012)
AUD and NZD out-yielded USD and JPY at every date from 2008-07 to 2016-12 (prior knowledge of RBA/RBNZ/Fed/BoJ policy rates; not re-opened here)
the premium is compensation for crash risk, so it should be earned in calm regimes
the spot legs of three positive-carry majors rise in calm regimes (R2A-1)
carry currencies keep falling for a week after VIX starts rising (R2A-2)
carry INCLUDING its interest income (rate-differential proxy, BIS policy rates) has positive net expectancy on 8 majors, 2008-2016 (R3-A/G/H): the income is smaller than the spot loss
carry on the JPY pairs: untestable under the frozen rule (no BoJ policy rate 2013-04 -> 2016-09)

nodes.summary: spot legs only (no carry income measurable): long AUDJPY/AUDUSD/NZDUSD while VIX < 20 -0.119R (n 263, P(direction) 45%); short after VIX rises -0.056R (n 475). The omitted income is estimated at +0.05-0.08R and would not change the sign

BIS policy rates, 8 pairs, 2008-07 -> 2017-01, carry income included as a RATE-DIFFERENTIAL CARRY PROXY: carry long -0.083R net (n 341; carry +0.045R, spot -0.101R gross, P(direction) 41%); while VIX < 20 -0.117R; without a recent policy move -0.044R

nodes.text: a currency whose relative interest rate rose tends to appreciate, not depreciate as UIP says
regressions of currency changes on the forward premium give the wrong sign for UIP (Fama 1984)
a CHANGE in the differential should be followed by appreciation of the currency it favours
with only US rates observable, the US 10y change stands in for the differential change (other rates near their floors in 2008-2016)
the next month's move follows last month's US-yield change (R2B)
the next month's move follows a widening, narrowing or accelerating policy-rate differential, or a recent policy move (R3-C/D/E/F)

nodes.summary: last month's US 10y change (> 10bp) as the differential change, 7 USD pairs: -0.108R (n 396, P(direction) 46%) and -0.061R (n 381, 51%): coin-flip direction
the true two-sided policy differential: widening -0.160R (n 149), narrowing -0.108R (n 218), accelerating +0.007R (n 249, t 0.10), after a policy move -0.151R (n 95)

source:Ferraro, Rogoff & Rossi, Can oil prices forecast exchange rates?, J. Int. Money and Finance 54 (2015)

nodes.text: a commodity exporter's currency moves with the price of its main export
the oil-CAD link is strong at daily frequency but contemporaneous; lagged oil does not forecast CAD out of sample (Ferraro et al. 2015)
a 20-day oil move predicts the next week of USDCAD at the required level (R2C)
a lagged effect in LARGE, persistent oil moves (2014-15): positive here, not distinguishable from one episode

nodes.summary: buy USDCAD after oil fell > 5%: +0.047R net (n 169, P(direction) 56%, t 0.77), mostly the 2014-15 oil collapse; the mirror -0.088R

nodes.id: source:Daniel & Moskowitz, Momentum crashes, J. Financial Economics 122 (2016)

nodes.text: momentum strategies lose most in panic states and sharp rebounds; calm states are safer
risk appetite (e.g. implied volatility) decides whether risky currencies are bought or dumped
equity momentum's worst losses occur in panic states and rebounds (Daniel & Moskowitz 2016)
the same crash mechanism applies to FX time-series momentum
restricting FX momentum to VIX < 20 produces a net edge on either side (R2D)
the SELL side of FX trend: positive but insignificant in four separate tests (CP-001-T2, CP-001-T4, SL-001-02, R2D-2), each dominated by one episode

nodes.summary: 12 pairs, 2008-07 -> 2017-01: BUY uptrends while calm -0.040R (n 593); SELL downtrends while calm +0.077R (n 581, t 0.85, passes cost/delay stress; fails significance, random, years, instruments, outliers: EURCHF 2015 dominates)
